I'd lower it to MEDIUM because the failure is conditional on deployment topology — on the ordinary single-canonical-domain production deploy window.location.origin and publicOrigin() are identical and nothing breaks; the damage requires the sheet to be printed from a preview/branch/non-canonical host. That is narrower than the app-wide, always-on exposure the other HIGHs describe.

evidence: public/sw.js:116-120 `function cachePut(cacheName, request, response) { if (!response || !response.ok || response.type === "opaque") return; const copy = response.clone(); caches.open(cacheName).then((c) => c.put(request, copy))... }` — no inspection of Cache-Control at all. Reached from the navigation branch (:161-162) and, for everything else same-origin GET, from :210-211 `const res = await fetch(request); cachePut(RUNTIME_CACHE, request, res);` with the offline replay at :214-215 `const cached = await caches.match(request); if (cached) return cached;`. app/api/share/file/route.ts:31 is a GET and :145-150 returns the stamped PDF with `"Cache-Control": "no-store"` — cached regardless.
note: Survives, and the download-url half is slightly worse than stated: grep for Cache-Control across app/api/storage/download-url/route.ts returns nothing, so the signed-URL JSON at :153 carries no cache directive at all rather than a no-store the SW overrides. Nothing clears Cache Storage on sign-out — the only caches.delete in the repo is the version sweep at sw.js:59-60, keyed on VERSION, and grep across app/components/lib finds no caches.* call outside a test — so RUNTIME_CACHE is device-wide and survives both sign-out and share revocation. caches.match keys on URL (headers other than Vary are not part of the key), so a second user on the shared tablet replays the first user's bytes.

evidence: app/api/data-export/run-scheduled/route.ts:60-66 — `.from("export_destinations").select("*").eq("enabled", true).not("next_run_at", "is", null).lte("next_run_at", nowIso).limit(50)` is the entire eligibility test; there is no join or lookup against orgs.subscription_status and none against org_members for dest.created_by. It then runs unconditionally at :107-115 `buildAndDeliverExport({ ... orgId: dest.org_id, exporterUserId: "cron", exporterEmail: "cron@manufacturing-os", includeFiles: dest.include_files ?? true, delivery: { kind: "destination", destination: dest } })`. evidence: lib/exportRunner.ts:72-75 `const { address } = await lookup(host); if (isPrivateIp(address)) throw ...` — a resolution wholly separate from the one the connection makes — followed at :308-312 by `const res = await fetch(dest.webhook_url, { method: "POST", headers, body: zipBytes as unknown as BodyInit });` with no `redirect` option, i.e. the spec default "follow".
